title: COMMON block declaration order IS the memory layout — reorder = silent corruption
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE LOAD_HEADER(X, Y, Z)
C     COMMON /HDR/ X, Y, Z places X at offset 0, Y at offset 4,
C     Z at offset 8 (assuming REAL*4). Another translation unit
C     declaring COMMON /HDR/ A(3) reads the same 12 bytes as an
C     array. Reordering the variables -- even putting them on
C     separate lines for clarity -- silently rewrites the layout
C     and any other unit reading /HDR/ now sees garbage.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      REAL X, Y, Z
      COMMON /HDR/ X, Y, Z
      X = 1.0
      Y = 2.0
      Z = 3.0
      RETURN
      END
notes: COMMON-block layout is the most common silent-corruption migration trap. A modernised port that turns /HDR/ into a Record class with named fields must respect declaration order EVERYWHERE the block is consumed. The spec must flag the order-dependency AND ask the SME to enumerate every consumer of the block.
